name: NKDB Visual Atlas: Geolocated Detention & Incident Map Dataset
publisher: Database Center for North Korean Human Rights (NKDB)
description: Interactive map dataset of 419 distinct detention, security, and human rights incident locations across North Korea and China border regions, with confirmation status and incident density counts.
coverage: 1960s–2024; North Korea national & China border regions
last_updated_evidence: Records in published payload have publishedAt and openedAt timestamps of 2025-12-19T15:53:20.519Z; copyright and asset versions updated 2025-2026.
update_cadence: Periodic annual/semi-annual releases from NKDB Unified Database
presentation: Rendered on a CARTO Dark Matter basemap using MapLibre GL markers with pulsing circles sized by incident strength. Good aesthetic design, but lacks direct GeoJSON download, coordinates are buried inside SvelteKit devalue serialization, and has bot mitigation that blocks standard curl.
build_idea: Ingest all 419 points directly into our /atlas map layer as 'Detention & Human Rights Incidents', categorized by facility type (Kwanliso, Kyohwaso, Jipkyolso, MPS, MSS, China border detention) with confirmation badges.
notes: Extracted full 419 records in probe script extract_visualatlas_locations.py. 62 prisons/camps, 52 MPS police stations, 44 MSS state security offices, 17 holding camps, 11 facilities in China, 62 victim houses, 171 other sites.

name: NKDB Visual Atlas: Human Rights Incidents Pool API
publisher: Database Center for North Korean Human Rights (NKDB)
description: Structured database of 3,636 verified human rights violations occurring in the North Korean penal and state security systems, categorized by legal right, decade, perpetrator body, and location taxonomy.
last_updated_evidence: Incidents table contains timestamps through late December 2025 (publishedAt: 2025-12-19T15:53:20.519Z).
presentation: Paginated incident cards with filters by right violated, perpetrator agency, and decade. Detailed witness narrative summaries, but no bulk download button.
build_idea: Join incident records to our atlas points via the slug/location foreign key, allowing users clicking a camp or police station to read the actual witness testimonies and legal violations recorded there.
notes: Verified endpoint with custom payload in probe_visualatlas_deep.mjs. Returns 2.58 MB JSON response with 3,636 total rows. Fields: incidentId, damageDescription, rights, perpetrator, decade, sourceDescription, location, relatedLinks.

name: NKDB Visual Atlas: DPRK Penal & Legal Terminology Pool API
publisher: Database Center for North Korean Human Rights (NKDB)
description: Comprehensive bilingual dictionary of 770 terms explaining North Korea's penal architecture, legal codes, security apparatus designations, and slang used by detainees and security officers.
coverage: Historical to contemporary DPRK penal lexicon
last_updated_evidence: Payload fetched in probe returns total=770 items with recent schema revision hash.
presentation: Alphabetical and Korean syllable indexed accordion on visualatlas.org. High quality definitions with citations to DPRK criminal law and international treaties.
build_idea: Build a pop-up glossary on hover for terms like 'Kwanliso', 'Kyo-hwa-so', 'Jip-gyeol-so', 'Rodong-danryeon-dae', 'Daekisil' in our atlas and articles.
notes: Verified in probe_visualatlas_deep.mjs. Total 770 entries; fields include title, content, reference, indexNumber, indexKo, indexEn.

name: North Korean Prison Database (NKPD): Penal Facilities Dataset
publisher: Korea Future (in partnership with HURIDOCS)
description: Comprehensive investigative database of 245 documented North Korean penal facilities, detailing facility types, administering agencies (MPS vs MSS), jurisdictional level, and exact GPS coordinates for 103 facilities.
last_updated_evidence: Entity editDate fields in Uwazi REST response reflect regular maintenance into 2024; Korea Future annual updates.
presentation: Uwazi web catalog with province-level aggregation cards, filtering by facility type (Daekisil, Jipkyolso, Kuryujang, Rodong Kyoyangdae/Danryondae), and individual facility dossiers. Clean interface, open REST API.
build_idea: Import all 103 geolocated facilities and merge the remaining 142 province-level facilities into our master atlas layer, establishing the most authoritative open database of ordinary detention centers and holding camps.
notes: Verified endpoint and fetched all 245 records in probe_nkpd_api.mjs and nkpd_facilities.json. 103 facilities contain precise lat/lon in metadata.geolocation_geolocation.

name: Korea Future: 3D Architectural Reconstructions of DPRK Detention Centres
publisher: Korea Future
description: Detailed 3D architectural models of Onsong County MPS Detention Centre and North Hamgyong MPS Holding Centre built using survivor testimonies, photogrammetry, and commercial satellite imagery.
last_updated_evidence: Presented on nkpd.io with 3D walkthrough engine; documented in Korea Future 2023 penal system reports.
presentation: Interactive WebGL/Three.js 3D facility models allowing users to inspect interrogation cells, solitary confinement rooms, guard posts, and exterior perimeters.
build_idea: Embed 3D spatial interactive viewers or thumbnail links inside the facility drawer for Onsong Detention Centre and North Hamgyong Holding Camp.
notes: Accessible on nkpd.io under 3D Model navigation tabs (Onsong County MPS Detention Centre and North Hamgyong MPS Holding Centre).

name: HRNK: North Korea Prison Camp Location Map (Google My Maps KML)
publisher: Committee for Human Rights in North Korea (HRNK)
description: Geospatial dataset compiled by HRNK identifying 24 key political prison camps (Kwan-li-so) and long-term reeducation camps (Kyo-hwa-so) with coordinates, operational status, and provincial locations.
last_updated_evidence: Google My Maps metadata and copyright 2024 on nkhiddengulag.org; includes recent updates to Camp 25 and closed status for Camp 22.
update_cadence: Updated when major research reports or satellite reviews are published
presentation: Embedded Google My Maps iframe on nkhiddengulag.org. Simple point markers with camp names and province descriptions, but lacks detailed facility outlines.
build_idea: Use as a primary ground truth validation dataset to cross-check our Kwan-li-so and Kyo-hwa-so atlas points.
notes: Downloaded full KML (49 KB) in probe hrnk_camps.kml. 4 Operational Kwanliso (14, 15, 16, 25), 2 Closed Kwanliso (18, 22), 4 Operational Kyohwaso (1, 4, 12, 6), 2 Closed Kyohwaso (22, 77), 12 Unconfirmed Probable camps.

name: HRNK: Commercial Satellite Imagery Camp Analysis Report Series
publisher: Committee for Human Rights in North Korea (HRNK)
description: Monographic series of multi-year high-resolution satellite imagery investigations of individual prison camps, documenting facility boundaries, guard towers, coal mines, crematoria, and security perimeters with exact imagery dates.
last_updated_evidence: Kwan-li-so No. 25 Update 4 published in 2024; earlier reports between 2012 and 2021 by Joseph S. Bermudez Jr. et al.
license: All rights reserved (HRNK / AllSource Analysis / Maxar)
presentation: Rich, multi-page PDF reports containing annotated Maxar/DigitalGlobe satellite plates with imagery timestamps, spatial coordinate tables, and perimeter polygon maps.
build_idea: Digitize the camp boundary polygons, guard tower locations, and perimeter fences from each report into our MapLibre atlas.
notes: Verified report URLs on hrnk.org and nkhiddengulag.org. Key authors: Joseph S. Bermudez Jr., Greg Scarlatoiu, Amanda Mortwedt Oh, Andy Dinville, Mike Eley.

name: TJWG: Mapping the Fate of the Dead: Killings and Burials in North Korea
publisher: Transitional Justice Working Group (TJWG)
description: Pioneering geospatial investigation documenting 318 state-sanctioned execution sites, 47 burial and cremation locations, and government offices holding potential records based on interviews with 610 defectors.
coverage: 1960s–2019; North Korea nationwide (heavy Ryanggang & North Hamgyong concentration)
last_updated_evidence: Report published June 2019; methodology expanded in subsequent Kim Jong-un era reports (2021, 2026).
presentation: PDF report with clustered GIS maps, heatmaps, and environmental terrain breakdowns (riverbeds, hillsides, school fields). Precise GPS coordinates are intentionally withheld from public release to prevent regime tampering with mass graves.
build_idea: Display county-level choropleth and cluster pins representing execution and burial density, respecting TJWG's evidence protection protocol while educating users on the geography of public executions.
notes: TJWG web portal protected by Deflect challenge. Report confirmed via publication metadata. Defector interview sample: 610 people.

name: TJWG: Mapping North Korea's Executions Before and After COVID-19
publisher: Transitional Justice Working Group (TJWG)
description: Updated spatial analysis of 144 execution cases and death sentencings, detailing 46 execution sites utilized during Kim Jong-un's reign and spatial displacement away from urban centers.
last_updated_evidence: Published April 2026 covering Kim Jong-un era 2011–2024 data.
presentation: Comprehensive PDF with geospatial diagrams, satellite imagery overlays of execution airfields and riverbanks, and statistical analyses of border quarantine crackdowns.
build_idea: Create a timeline filter on execution sites showing how Kim Jong-un altered execution geography away from public markets toward controlled perimeter zones.
notes: Verified via TJWG research release in April 2026.

name: Curtis Melvin / 38 North: North Korea Uncovered (Google Earth KMZ)
publisher: Curtis Melvin (North Korean Economy Watch / US-Korea Institute at SAIS / 38 North)
description: The foundational crowdsourced Google Earth mapping project for North Korea, containing thousands of annotated placemarks including extensive coverage of political prison camp boundaries, guard posts, and mine shafts.
last_updated_evidence: Final official release version 18 published April 2012 on NK Economy Watch.
presentation: Packed Google Earth KMZ with hundreds of nested subfolders. Requires Google Earth Pro desktop; can cause UI lag if all layers are toggled simultaneously.
build_idea: Extract the camp boundary polygons and security perimeter vectors (Camp 14, 15, 16, 18, 22) into GeoJSON to serve as vector polygon overlays on our MapLibre atlas.
notes: NKEconwatch website protected by Cloudflare Turnstile. Succeeded by Jacob Bogle's AccessDPRK and 38 North Digital Atlas.

name: Jacob Bogle: #AccessDPRK Mapping Project
publisher: Jacob Bogle
description: Comprehensive successor to North Korea Uncovered, mapping over 50,000 installations across North Korea, featuring dedicated layers for penal facilities, labor camps, border security outposts, and military installations.
last_updated_evidence: Continuous updates posted on blogspot and personal site; 2025/2026 map editions released.
license: Free version available for personal/research use; Pro version for commercial
presentation: Tiered Google Earth KMZ files with detailed annotations, historical imagery comparison notes, and categorized folder hierarchies.
build_idea: Extract detention-related layers (penal labor camps, border holding centers) to expand our non-kwanliso detention coverage.
notes: Verified via author blogspot (mynorthkorea.blogspot.com) and OSINT research community.

name: Wikipedia / Wikidata: North Korean Concentration Camps Dataset
publisher: Wikimedia Foundation
description: Structured encyclopedia articles and linked Wikidata items for 23 North Korean concentration camps and prisons, containing coordinates for 11 major facilities and leaving 12 un-geocoded.
last_updated_evidence: Live query via MediaWiki API returns current revision coordinates and Wikidata Q-IDs.
presentation: Standard Wikipedia articles with infoboxes and OpenStreetMap coordinate popups. Several major facilities lack coordinates completely (e.g. Chungsan, Hamhung, Kanggye, Onsong, Oro).
build_idea: Cross-reference Wikipedia links in our atlas drawers and upstream our verified coordinates back to Wikidata/Wikipedia to resolve the 12 missing coordinate entries.
notes: Verified in probe_wikipedia_coords.py and wikipedia_camp_coordinates.json. Verified coordinates: Chongjin (41.833, 129.726), Chongori (42.210, 129.754), Hoeryong (42.538, 129.936), Hwasong (41.269, 129.391), Kaechon (39.571, 126.055), Yodok (39.674, 126.851).

name: UN Commission of Inquiry on Human Rights in the DPRK (COI) Final Report & Satellite Annexes
publisher: United Nations Human Rights Council
description: Landmark 372-page UN report documenting crimes against humanity in North Korea, with Chapter IV.C detailing the Kwanliso political prison camp system, Kyohwaso ordinary prison system, and UNOSAT commercial satellite imagery comparisons.
last_updated_evidence: Official UN document date A/HRC/25/CRP.1, published 7 February 2014.
presentation: Comprehensive PDF with satellite imagery plates, camp diagrams, witness sketches, and systematic legal analysis of extermination, murder, torture, and forced labor.
build_idea: Extract official UN legal findings and witness testimony quotes to include in our camp details drawer, establishing UN credibility for our atlas markers.
notes: Permanent UN document URL verified via docs.un.org/a/hrc/25/crp.1.

name: Amnesty International: North Korea Political Prison Camps Satellite Imagery Analysis
publisher: Amnesty International
description: Series of technical satellite briefings (2011, 2013, 2016) monitoring infrastructure changes, perimeter expansions, housing demolitions, and industrial activity at Kwanliso 15 (Yodok), 16 (Hwasong), and 25 (Chongjin).
last_updated_evidence: Amnesty International public briefing published November 2016 analyzing Camp 25 expansion.
presentation: Web multimedia feature and PDF briefings with side-by-side satellite comparisons and analysis by imagery experts.
build_idea: Use Amnesty's before/after satellite findings to illustrate physical changes in camp infrastructure over time (e.g. Camp 25 perimeter expansion) in camp explainer articles.
notes: Verified via Amnesty International document archive.

name: CSIS Beyond Parallel: North Korea Satellite Imagery & Prison Labor Research
publisher: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
description: Remote-sensing analyses examining the intersection of North Korea's penal camps and national economic infrastructure projects, such as the Orangchon Hydroelectric Power Station bordering Camp 16.
last_updated_evidence: Articles and imagery updates published regularly on beyondparallel.csis.org.
presentation: Interactive web articles with high-resolution satellite imagery callouts, annotated overlays, and expert geopolitical analysis.
build_idea: Link camp facilities to nearby economic infrastructure (e.g. mines, power plants, railways) on our map to demonstrate how prison labor is integrated into the state economy.
notes: Verified via search and CSIS publication index. Bermudez co-authored multiple studies on Beyond Parallel.

name: ROK Ministry of Unification: North Korea Human Rights Report (북한인권보고서)
publisher: Ministry of Unification, Republic of Korea (북한인권기록센터)
description: Comprehensive annual official Korean government investigation based on testimonies of over 1,600 defectors, providing detailed accounts of the multi-tier detention hierarchy (Kwanliso, Kyohwaso, Jipkyolso, Rodong-danryeon-dae, Kuryujang).
last_updated_evidence: Annual publication cycle mandated by North Korean Human Rights Act; published annually 2023–2026.
license: Korea Open Government License (KOGL Type 1 - Open)
presentation: Massive 500+ page official government report available in Korean and English PDF. Contains exhaustive narrative sections, legal classification charts, and defector testimony citations.
build_idea: Synthesize the official South Korean government taxonomy of detention tiers (Kwanliso vs Kyohwaso vs Jipkyolso vs Danryeondae) into our site structure and filter dropdowns.
notes: Publicly released annually under ROK North Korean Human Rights Act. Verified via Ministry of Unification portal.

name: KINU: White Paper on Human Rights in North Korea (북한인권백서)
publisher: Korea Institute for National Unification (통일연구원)
description: The benchmark annual scholarly assessment of human rights conditions in North Korea, featuring authoritative tables tracking active vs closed political prison camps (Kwanliso) and numbered correctional facilities (Kyohwaso).
last_updated_evidence: 2024 and 2025 White Papers published in KINU repository.
presentation: Authoritative annual book available as free PDF in both Korean and English. Contains tabular summaries of detention facilities, prisoner numbers, and administrative oversight.
build_idea: Adopt KINU's authoritative operational status classification (e.g. confirmation that Camp 14, 16, 18, 25 are active, while Camp 15 and 22 are closed) as the primary status toggle in our atlas.
notes: Verified via KINU publication portal and research findings. Established that Camp 15 (Yodok) closed circa 2019-2020.

name: NHRCK: Survey on North Korean Political Prison Camps (북한 정치범수용소 실태조사)
publisher: National Human Rights Commission of Korea (국가인권위원회)
description: In-depth landmark investigation into the internal layout, division of labor, total control vs revolutionizing zones, and daily regimes of Camp 14, 15, 18, and 22 based on exhaustive defector interviews.
last_updated_evidence: Published January 2010 by NHRCK research team.
presentation: Extensive academic report with detailed hand-drawn maps by survivors, administrative hierarchy diagrams, and zone layout maps.
build_idea: Use the internal sub-camp diagrams (villages, security gates, mining pits) to flesh out the detail pages for Kwanliso 14, 15, 18, and 22.
notes: Verified in NHRCK public research archive.

name: Sukuukai (救う会): Testimony Archive on Japanese Abductees in DPRK Prison Camps
publisher: National Association for the Rescue of Japanese Kidnapped by North Korea (救う会)
description: Extensive Japanese-language repository of survivor and former guard testimonies detailing the presence of Japanese abductees and Zainichi Korean repatriates in Camp 15 (Yodok), Camp 18 (Bukchang), and Camp 22 (Hoeryong).
last_updated_evidence: Active updates on sukuukai.jp homepage and newsletter.
presentation: Classic web 1.0 Japanese text archive organized by abductee names, defector testimony dates, and symposium records.
build_idea: Add a 'Foreign / Abductee Detainees' tag to relevant camp profiles (Yodok, Bukchang, Sunghori) linking Japanese-language survivor records.
notes: Verified on sukuukai.jp. Includes detailed testimonies of former guard Ahn Myong-chol and defector Kang Chol-hwan.

name: COMJAN: Suspected Abduction and Detention Points Archive (特定失踪者問題調査会)
publisher: Investigation Commission on Missing Japanese Probably Related to North Korea (特定失踪者問題調査会)
description: Japanese investigative project led by Kazuhiro Araki mapping suspected maritime abduction departure points and internal detention facilities where missing Japanese citizens are believed held.
last_updated_evidence: Active investigative reports and missing person case files updated monthly in 2026.
presentation: HTML case profiles with GPS departure coordinates in Japan and estimated destination detention points inside the DPRK.
build_idea: Map the maritime abduction corridor connecting Japanese coastal abduction points to North Korean intake security facilities (Chongjin, Wonsan, Nampo).
notes: Verified via chousakai.jp investigation database.

name: Asia Press / Rimjin-gang: Underground Reporting on North Korea's Penal System
publisher: Asia Press International (Jiro Ishimaru)
description: Covert in-country investigative reporting by North Korean citizen journalists documenting the operation of labor training camps (단련대), quarantine detention facilities, and public execution orders under the anti-reactionary thought law.
last_updated_evidence: Weekly undercover dispatches published in Japanese and Korean on asiapress.org in 2026.
presentation: High quality investigative journalism articles containing covert audio recordings, smuggling photographs, official directive transcripts, and county-level reporting.
build_idea: Cite recent Asia Press dispatches in our camp and holding center pages to provide up-to-date qualitative context on current penal conditions.
notes: Verified via Asia Press website. Chief editor Jiro Ishimaru.

name: OpenStreetMap (OSM) DPRK Prison & Administrative Feature Extract
publisher: OpenStreetMap Contributors / Geofabrik GmbH
description: Daily-updated complete OpenStreetMap database extract for North Korea, containing community-mapped prison polygons, perimeter fences, watchtowers, and administrative boundaries (amenity=prison, boundary=prison_camp).
last_updated_evidence: Verified HTTP header Last-Modified: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 23:55:22 GMT; file size 92,390,860 bytes.
license: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL 1.0)
presentation: Standard OSM binary PBF and ESRI Shapefile formats. High geometry precision for mapped facilities, but tags and coverage are uneven.
build_idea: Extract existing OSM prison ways and relations to render detailed camp perimeter fence lines and building footprints on our MapLibre map.
notes: Verified download size (88.1 MB) and Last-Modified date via curl header check.

name: Namu.wiki: North Korean Penal Facilities & Political Prison Camps Portal
publisher: Namu.wiki Community
description: Extremely detailed Korean-language crowdsourced intelligence compiling facility numbers, historic redesignations, administrative boundary changes, defector account cross-references, and satellite coordinates for North Korean prisons.
last_updated_evidence: Live wiki revision history shows edits in September 2026.
presentation: Dense hypertext wiki with extensive citations to ROK court cases, defector memoirs, satellite coordinates, and Ministry of Unification reports.
build_idea: Mine Namu.wiki's extensive cross-references for Korean-language facility nicknames, former camp numbers (e.g. Camp 11, 12, 13, 26, 27), and closure dates.
notes: Covers distinct pages for 관리소, 교화소, 집결소, 노동단련대, and specific camp entries.

name: Human Rights Watch: "Worth Less Than An Animal": Pre-trial Detention & Holding Centres
publisher: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
description: Comprehensive report investigating the opaque pre-trial detention system (kuryujang) and holding centers (jipkyolso), detailing systemic torture, forced confessions, and detention pipeline geography.
last_updated_evidence: Official publication date October 19, 2020.
presentation: Interactive multimedia report and PDF with defector diagrams of cell layouts, interrogation seating, and intake procedural flows.
build_idea: Create an interactive 'Path through the Penal System' explainer showing how a captured border-crosser is transferred from China -> MSS border post -> Jipkyolso -> Kuryujang -> Kyohwaso/Kwanliso.
notes: Verified on hrw.org. Key focus on MPS/MSS pre-trial detention facilities.

name: David Hawk / HRNK: The Hidden Gulag & The Parallel Gulag
publisher: Committee for Human Rights in North Korea (HRNK)
description: The seminal research series (Vol. 1 2003, Vol. 2 2012, and 'The Parallel Gulag' 2017) that first documented the dual architecture of MSS Kwanliso and MPS Kyohwaso, matching survivor sketches with satellite plates.
last_updated_evidence: 'The Parallel Gulag' published October 2017; foundational Hidden Gulag volumes 2003 and 2012.
presentation: Comprehensive print/PDF books with high quality satellite imagery plates, victim affidavits, camp blueprints, and system-wide structural charts.
build_idea: Incorporate David Hawk's historical camp facility numbering system and early baseline maps as a foundational reference layer.
notes: Verified on hrnk.org and nkhiddengulag.org.

name: Daily NK: North Korean Penal System & Camp Relocation Reporting
publisher: Daily NK
description: Continuous covert journalism from an extensive inside-North Korea informant network reporting on camp expansions, prisoner relocations, new border detention centres, and Ministry of Social Security policy changes.
last_updated_evidence: Daily articles published in Korean and English throughout 2026.
presentation: Standard digital news site with real-time news feeds, keyword search, and specialized coverage of internal security directives.
build_idea: Build a live RSS or feed parser filtering Daily NK stories tagged with detention facilities to flag operational shifts at specific camps.
notes: Verified via Daily NK web platform. Primary source for ground-level closures and relocations.

name: RENK: Pioneer Hand-Drawn Camp Maps & Border Facility Documentation
publisher: Rescue the North Korean People! Urgent Action Network (RENK / 救え！北朝鮮の民衆/緊急行動ネットワーク)
description: Historic Japanese-Korean human rights initiative led by Prof. Lee Young-hwa that collected the earliest defector hand-drawn maps of Camp 14, 15, and 22, and first documented the border holding facilities in Musan and Onsong.
last_updated_evidence: Historic web archive maintained online.
presentation: Early web archive containing scanned survivor sketches, audio interviews, and video stills from smuggled VHS tapes.
build_idea: Include historical survivor hand-drawn sketches alongside modern satellite imagery in camp deep-dive pages to show how defectors originally described these spaces from memory.
notes: Verified via RENK Japanese web portal.

name: NKDB: White Paper on North Korean Human Rights
publisher: Database Center for North Korean Human Rights (NKDB)
description: Annual statistical compendium aggregating all cases documented in NKDB's Unified Database, analyzing the distribution of violations by facility type, administering agency, and year.
last_updated_evidence: Annual White Paper published in October 2025 by NKDB research institute.
presentation: Heavy statistical book with hundreds of tables, bar charts, and administrative province breakdowns of rights violations.
build_idea: Extract historical trendlines of detention facility violations by decade to render timeline charts in our /learn articles.
notes: Underlying data source for Visual Atlas and Larchiveum.
